correctness.rationale: The twelve-vertex graph is explicitly given by thirty edges of a two-pentagon icosahedral realization. Every perfect matching is enumerated by exhaustive least-unmatched-vertex recursion. A pair of matchings is adjacent exactly when its symmetric difference is connected and 2-regular on four or six distinct vertices. Direct full pairwise comparison therefore produces every and only the allowed alternating-cycle flips, including chorded cycles. The exact graph has 125 perfect matchings. There are 300 four-cycle flip edges with component sizes (120,1,1,1,1,1) and a giant-component radius/diameter (5,6), and 580 six-cycle edges with one component, radius 3, diameter 4. The five isolated four-cycle states coincide exactly with all five six-cycle centers, the remaining 120 six-cycle eccentricities being four. A second program independently scans all 593775 edge six-subsets and explicitly enumerates/toggles alternating 4/6-cycles; complete canonical edge lists agree under SHA-256, with independently recomputed all-state BFS. Both programs were run and their exact outputs are included, along with three whole-state certificates. No inference from a partial enumeration is used.

originality.rationale: The existing icosahedral matching-complex calculation has the already known perfect-matching count 125, which this claim does not present as novel. Its homotopy theorem on the complex does not imply a four- or six-cycle transition graph on its top-dimensional simplices. The 2019 reconfiguration paper studies length-four flips and algorithmic complexity for graph classes, without resolving this icosahedral component census or length-six eccentricities. The 2026 decorated-graph results yield general connectivity bounds for particular constructions, not this exact icosahedral threshold and coincidence of frozen states with graph centers. The earlier 2014 anti-forcing paper concerns alternating cycles, mostly for planar bipartite graphs; the icosahedron is nonbipartite. Other historical examples enumerate different graphs and cannot imply this result by their statements. The public-record and primary-literature searches produced no stronger or equivalent exact table; unindexed graph-specific work is a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The regular icosahedron is a canonical planar triangulation with exclusively triangular (odd) faces, so facial even-cycle dimer moves are unavailable. Its shortest non-facial alternating-cycle moves provide a mathematically motivated natural test case for ergodic matching reconfiguration. The exact result identifies a nontrivial sharp move length, a 120-state connected class and five frozen states at length four, full connectivity at length six, and the unexpected fact that exactly those five frozen states become the unique graph centers under six-cycle dynamics. This describes a structural mobility reversal, not merely a known matching total or a routine parameter increment. The finite classification is self-contained and valuable as a benchmark, without asserting a general theorem.
